input.quote: 9.5 Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.
input.rationale: Section 9 provides only for-cause (9.1), insolvency (9.2) and Vendor-default/security (9.3) termination rights, and there is no 9.4; nothing in Sections 8 (three-year term, 180-day renewal notice), 10.2, 11 or 27.3 gives Customer a no-fault exit. A search for "convenience"/"without cause" returns no termination right for either Party. With a three-year Agreement term and auto-renewing Order Forms, the absence of any Customer convenience right falls below the fallback (60–90 days' notice) and into walk-away territory. Vendor likewise has no convenience right, so only the Customer-side gap needs fixing. We propose new 9.4 at the preferred position: 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no penalty, and confirmation that Vendor has no mid-term convenience right.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination and no early-termination fee or other penalty applies. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a term.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a Customer termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, as our playbook requires an exit in any term longer than twelve months; the three-year term in Section 8.1 currently offers no no-fault exit. If helpful, we can move to 60 days' notice as a fallback.
proposal.summary: Add Section 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience termination right with pro-rata refund and no Vendor convenience right.
